candidate_requirements.description: Candidate must maintain distinguishable self-state and other-state representations or auditable state components.
Other-state must update from observed partner behavior rather than partner ID, labels, fixture names, or evaluator-only fields.
Candidate must expose update traces, state snapshots, or hashes sufficient for replay and intervention audit.
Candidate must predict partner behavior under changed conditions before observing the response.
Candidate must update behavior after partner policy or preference shifts following interaction history.
Candidate action selection must depend on inferred other-state and not only on visible tokens or static lookup.
Candidate behavior must be recomputable from serialized state plus observation under the declared replay inputs.
Candidate must degrade meaningfully when the social-latent update path is disabled, frozen, shuffled, or corrupted under real rerun.

allowed_representation_note: Explicit, learned, or high-dimensional latent states are allowed only if update history, state snapshots or hashes, replay inputs, intervention effects, leakage boundary, and baseline comparisons are auditable.
blocking_conditions: other-state is keyed by partner ID
candidate receives evaluator-only target or partner-type fields
candidate has query or feedback access denied to fair baselines
candidate state cannot be serialized for replay recomputation
candidate behavior is unaffected by social-latent update ablation
candidate behavior is a fixed behavior tree over visible tokens only
